title: Term calendar
description: The academic calendar for one FSU term: when classes run, when the deadlines fall, which days are off, and when finals happen. Static shipped data, one record per term, joined to everything else by termCode. It is the piece that turns a weekly recurring schedule into actual dates, so "what's due this week?" and "is there class on Monday?" both bottom out here. Every deadline carries a machine-readable type so that deadlines can be filtered without string matching on their descriptions, and every dated entry is an ISO-8601 date in America/New_York, with an optional wall-clock time for deadlines that expire partway through the day.

termCode.description: The term this calendar describes. Primary key.

displayName.description: How FSU names the term in prose, for example "Fall 2026".

timezone.description: The timezone every date and time in this record is interpreted in. Fixed to a single value because all FSU campuses observe US Eastern time. It is stated explicitly rather than assumed so that a consumer converting to absolute instants has the zone in hand, and so that daylight-saving transitions during the term are resolved against a named zone rather than a fixed offset.

startDate.description: First official day of the term as the university defines it, which may precede the first day of classes.

endDate.description: Last official day of the term, normally the end of finals or commencement.

classesBeginDate.description: First day classes actually meet. This, not startDate, is what a recurring meeting expands from.

classesEndDate.description: Last day of regular classes, before reading days and finals. Recurring meetings stop here.

deadlines.description: Dated deadlines for the term. The array is heterogeneous by design and is meant to be filtered on the type field, never parsed out of descriptions.

nonClassDays.description: Days and ranges when regular classes do not meet: holidays, breaks, reading days, and full campus closures. A recurring meeting must be suppressed on any date covered here, which is the main reason this record is needed to answer scheduling questions at all.

finals.description: The final examination period. Kept as its own object rather than as a nonClassDays entry because classes do not meet but the campus is at its busiest, and exam blocks do not follow the term's normal meeting pattern.

sessions.description: Sub-sessions within the term, which supply the date ranges that a course meeting's partOfTerm value refers to. Without these, two courses in the same time slot in different parts of a term look like a conflict when they never overlap. An EMPTY array is ambiguous on its own — it cannot distinguish a term that genuinely has no sub-sessions from one whose ranges nobody has been able to find — so sessionsStatus, not the length of this array, is what a consumer must branch on.

sessionsStatus.description: Whether this term's sub-session date ranges could be established, and therefore whether a course meeting's partOfTerm can be resolved to dates at all. This field exists because the failure is silent otherwise: an empty sessions array looks exactly like a term with no half-terms, and a consumer that cannot tell the two apart will confidently report "no conflict" for two courses whose real dates it does not know. "published" means the university publishes the ranges and they are transcribed into sessions, which must then be non-empty. "not-published" means the university's calendar for this term does not state them; sessions is empty and every non-full-term partOfTerm value in this term is UNRESOLVABLE. This is the state of the Fall 2026 record shipped with this plugin: the Registrar publishes session breakdowns for summer terms only. "not-checked" means nobody has looked; treat it exactly as cautiously as "not-published". See the RESOLUTION RULE on course-meeting.schema.json's partOfTerm for what a consumer must do in each case.

parkingBlackouts.description:
Dates within this term on which the parking rules in parking-zones.json are KNOWN TO BE WRONG and must not be evaluated. It lives on the term calendar rather than on a zone because a blackout closes an unknown set of areas across the whole campus at once, so attaching it to any one zone would understate it.

REFUSAL RULE. Before answering any question about parking on a date, a consumer MUST check that date against this array. If it matches, the consumer REFUSES: it states that FSU closes and reserves campus parking on that date, that it does not know which areas, and that the student must check FSU Transportation & Parking Services. It does NOT answer and hedge, and it does NOT fall back to the ordinary rules. This is deliberately asymmetric with the rest of the dataset, where a low-confidence answer is still an answer, and the reason is the consequence: FSU's own game-day page says a vehicle left in a reserved area "will be towed at your expense". A hedged wrong answer and a confident wrong answer end the same way.

This array deliberately does NOT encode what the rules become on these dates. FSU does not publish that, so any such rule would be invention. Recording only the dates is the whole of what can be sourced, and it is enough to refuse safely. An empty array does not mean there are no blackouts, only that none were sourced.

source.description: Which published FSU academic calendar this was transcribed from and when. Calendars are revised, so an answer about a deadline should hedge when this is old.

provenance.description: Per-record audit trail: which page this record was read from, on what date, by what method, and how much to trust it. REQUIRED on every shipped record. A record that cannot name a source it was actually fetched from, or a documented computation over records that were, does not belong in the data directory at all; it belongs in DATA-GAPS.md.

deadlineType.description: A closed set of deadline kinds so deadlines can be filtered programmatically. The two a student asks about most are "drop-add", the end of the add/drop window at the start of term, and "course-withdrawal", the last day to withdraw from a single course; "term-withdrawal" is the different and heavier act of withdrawing from every course. "drop-without-penalty" is kept separate from "course-withdrawal" because dropping inside the early window leaves no transcript mark while withdrawing later does. Use "other" only when no listed type fits, and put the specifics in description.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the term.

date.description: The day the deadline falls on, in America/New_York.

time.description: Wall-clock time the deadline expires, when it is not end of day. Many FSU deadlines expire at "23:59" and some administrative ones at "17:00". When absent, treat the deadline as expiring at the end of the stated date, and say so rather than implying a precision the data does not have.

description.description: The deadline in the university's own words, for the student to read.

appliesToSession.description: The code of the session in this term's sessions array that the deadline applies to. Omit for a deadline that applies to the whole term. Half-term and summer-session courses have their own, much earlier, drop and withdrawal dates, and applying the full-term date to them is a costly error.

url.description: Link to the official page describing this deadline or the form that satisfies it.

nonClassPeriod.description: A day or run of days when classes do not meet. Single days are expressed with startDate and endDate equal.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the term.

name.description: What the period is called, for example "Thanksgiving Break" or "Labor Day".

type.description: The kind of non-class period. "holiday" is an observed university holiday; "break" is a multi-day recess such as spring break; "reading-day" is the study day between the end of classes and finals, when classes do not meet but the campus is open; "no-class-day" covers days classes are cancelled while offices stay open; "campus-closed" means buildings are shut, which also makes every parking and routing answer moot; "emergency-closure" covers hurricane and weather closures added after publication.

startDate.description: First day of the period, inclusive.

endDate.description: Last day of the period, inclusive. Equal to startDate for a single day.

classesCancelled.description: Whether regular classes are suppressed for the WHOLE of these dates. Nearly always true; false exists for days that are administratively notable but on which classes still meet. False does NOT mean the day is ordinary: see cancelledFromTime, which covers the half-day case that this boolean alone cannot express.

cancelledFromTime.description: Wall-clock time from which classes are cancelled on a PARTIAL day, in America/New_York. Present only when classesCancelled is false and the day is nonetheless not a normal one: FSU's Homecoming Friday cancels classes from 12:00 p.m. onward while morning classes meet as usual. Before this field existed the only way to record that was to put it in the name and set classesCancelled to false, which understates the day and reads to any consumer as "classes meet normally" -- a student is then told to walk to a 2 p.m. class that is not happening. A consumer MUST treat a day carrying this field as three-valued (classes meet / classes meet until this time / no classes) rather than as a boolean. Omit for a whole-day cancellation, which is what classesCancelled true already says.

campusClosed.description: Whether buildings are closed too. Distinct from classesCancelled: on a reading day classes do not meet but the library is full.

finalsPeriod.description: The final examination period for the term. Kept as its own object rather than as a nonClassDays entry because classes do not meet but the campus is at its busiest, and exam blocks do not follow the term's normal meeting pattern. NOTE that this object holds the exam WEEK, not the exam GRID: it has nowhere to put "the Tuesday 09:05 lecture sits its final at 15:00 on Thursday". url is therefore the only route to a student's actual exam times, and a consumer must send them there rather than expanding their weekly schedule across these dates.

note.description: How exam times are assigned, and where the official exam grid is published. Exam blocks generally do not fall at the course's normal meeting time, so a schedule expanded from weekly meetings is wrong for this week and an answer should say so rather than guess.

url.description: Link to the published final exam schedule.

session.description: A sub-session of the term, supplying the dates that a course meeting's partOfTerm refers to. Only present when the term record's sessionsStatus is "published".

code.description: Session identifier, drawn from the same value set as a course meeting's partOfTerm so the two join directly. The value "custom" is deliberately absent here: a custom range is stated on the meeting itself, not registered as a session.

name.description: Human-readable session name, for example "First Seven Weeks".

startDate.description: First day of classes in this session.

endDate.description: Last day of classes in this session.

parkingBlackout.description: One date on which normal parking rules do not apply and cannot be reconstructed.

date.description: The affected date. Note that these are not only weekends: a blackout can fall on an ordinary class day.

reason.description: Why the date is blacked out, so a refusal can say something more useful than "rules unavailable".

name.description: What is happening, in the source's own words, for the student to recognise — for example "Florida State vs. Clemson".

note.description: What the source did and did not say. In particular, whether any restriction is known to begin the night before.

sourceUrl.description: The page the date was read from.

allOf.title: Published sessions must actually be listed
allOf.description: sessionsStatus "published" is a claim that the ranges are in hand, so the array must not be empty. The reverse is also enforced: if sessions is empty the status cannot be "published". Nothing constrains "not-published" or "not-checked" beyond sessions being empty, which is their whole point.
